observed_failure_at_parent: thin() mutates the caller's bool array in place (input_modified: True) because the skeleton is created via np.asanyarray(image, dtype=bool).view(np.uint8), a memory-sharing view, and then overwritten during thinning; the project's regression test test_thin_copies_input[bool] FAILS at the parent.
verified: Both directions observed in container on bench-base:python-3.12. At parent_commit (git reset --hard 6baff20f; git clean -fdx): inspected skimage/morphology/_skeletonize.py line 324 'skel = np.asanyarray(image, dtype=bool).view(np.uint8)' (no .copy(), view shares memory with input, then 'skel[D] = 0' writes through it) and direct repro printed input_modified: True while the regression test failed (1 failed, 2 passed; only the bool param fails, float/int inputs get copied by the bool dtype conversion so are unaffected). After git reset --hard to fix_commit and rebuild, the same repro printed input_modified: False and the regression test passed 3/3. Note pytest ran with the regression test file checked out from the fix commit (git checkout <FIX> -- skimage/morphology/tests/test_skeletonize.py), per protocol.
install_recipe: apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config && pip install 'numpy==2.1.3' 'scipy==1.14.1' 'Cython<3.1' meson-python ninja pythran lazy-loader packaging networkx pillow imageio tifffile matplotlib pytest pytest-cov pytest-faulthandler pytest-doctestplus pytest-localserver pooch asv numpydoc && git config --global --add safe.directory /work/scikit-image && pip install -e . --no-build-isolation --config-settings=setup-args=-Dcpp_std=c++17
issue_paraphrase: Calling the binary image thinning function on a two-dimensional boolean image unexpectedly destroys the caller's array: pixels are erased from the input in place while the skeleton is being computed, so any code that reuses its mask afterwards silently gets a corrupted one. The function should leave the input untouched and return the skeleton in a freshly allocated array.
fix_summary: The upstream fix added a single .copy() so the uint8 view used for in-place thinning no longer aliases the caller's array (np.asanyarray(image, dtype=bool).copy().view(np.uint8)).
notes: Self-contained, no network, ~1 s test. Only bool-dtype input triggers the bug (float/int inputs are already copied during the bool conversion). Full scikit-image build from source is required (meson + Cython + pythran); see install_recipe. Build flag -Dcpp_std=c++17 is mandatory with pythran>=0.19 (skimage pins cpp_std=c++14 which fails to compile modern pythran headers). The bench-base image has no C compiler; install build-essential first.

issue_paraphrase: Fitting an ellipse to too few points gives the user no usable feedback. With exactly four arbitrary points the fit routine claims success and returns meaningless, made-up ellipse parameters, and with as few as three points it reports failure without any explanation of why. Fitting should refuse to proceed and clearly warn whenever fewer than five points are supplied, since five parameters are needed to determine an ellipse.
fix_summary: The upstream fix added an explicit len(data) < 5 check at the top of EllipseModel.estimate() that warns 'Need at least 5 data points to estimate an ellipse.' (RuntimeWarning) and returns False before any fitting math runs; it also fixed a typo in a comment.
notes: Self-contained, no network, <1 s test. The semantic difference for 4 arbitrary points (True with garbage params vs False with warning) is the strongest user-visible symptom; for 3 collinear points parent already returned False but without any warning. test_fit.py's other tests pass on the era deps; run only the named test to avoid noise from unrelated version-sensitive tests. Build notes from the thin entry apply identically (meson/cpp_std=c++17/build-essential).

observed_failure_at_parent: With cache=False, accessing RegionProperties (e.g. image_filled, area) still writes each computed property into the object's cache dict (len 3 after three accesses) even though caching was explicitly disabled, so the no-cache mode keeps holding computed arrays and memory. The project's regression test asserting the cache stays empty FAILS at the parent.
verified: Both directions observed in container on bench-base:python-3.12. At parent_commit (git reset --hard 9107d523; git clean -fdx): inspected the _cached decorator in _regionprops.py, where the guard 'if not ((prop in cache) and obj._cache_active): cache[prop] = f(obj)' still executes the cache write whenever the cache is inactive; direct repro printed cache size 3 with cache=False and the regression test (checked out from the fix commit) failed. After git reset --hard to fix_commit and rebuild, the same repro printed 0 and the regression test passed.
install_recipe: apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config && pip install 'numpy==2.1.3' 'scipy==1.14.1' 'Cython<3.1' meson-python ninja pythran lazy-loader packaging networkx pillow imageio tifffile matplotlib pytest pytest-cov pytest-faulthandler pytest-doctestplus pytest-localserver pooch asv numpydoc && git config --global --add safe.directory /work/scikit-image && pip install -e . --no-build-isolation --config-settings=setup-args=-Dcpp_std=c++17
issue_paraphrase: Turning off caching for region property computation does not actually stop caching: every property that is read while caching is disabled is still stored inside the region object, so the object keeps a growing private stash of computed arrays (and the memory they occupy) long after they were used. With caching disabled, no computed property should be retained.
fix_summary: The upstream fix restructured the _cached decorator so that when obj._cache_active is False it returns f(obj) directly without writing into the cache dict; when caching is on it only computes a property if it is not already cached.
notes: Self-contained, no network, <1 s test. The visible symptom is memory retention plus the failing regression test; returned property values are the same either way. test_regionprops.py is a bigger file (runs in ~15 s) but only the single named test needs to run. Build notes from the thin entry apply identically (meson/cpp_std=c++17/build-essential).

reproduction: cd <repo> && python -c "from skimage.measure.fit import _dynamic_max_trials; print(_dynamic_max_trials(1, 100, 1000, 1e-40))" -> parent prints -0.0, fix prints 1.0. pytest: python -m pytest 'skimage/measure/tests/test_fit.py::test_ransac_dynamic_max_trials_clipping' -p no:cacheprovider -q -> parent: 1 failed, fix: 1 passed.
observed_failure_at_parent: The RANSAC dynamic trial-count helper returns a non-positive number (-0.0) of maximum trials when the stopping probability is very small and/or the denominator approaches 1.0, e.g. _dynamic_max_trials(1, 100, 1000, 1e-40) == -0.0 instead of a positive integer. The project's regression test asserting positive trial counts FAILS at the parent.
verified: Both directions observed in container on bench-base:python-3.12. At parent_commit (git reset --hard f1892afb; git clean -fd): inspected fit.py _dynamic_max_trials, which only clips the denominator and clamps nom with max(_EPSILON, 1 - probability), so nom can round to exactly 1.0 and log(1)=0 produces a bogus 0/-0/negative trial count; direct repro printed -0.0 and the regression test (checked out from the fix commit) failed. After git reset --hard to fix_commit, the same repro printed 1.0 and the regression test passed. This change is contained in the pure-Python file skimage/measure/fit.py, so no recompilation is needed when switching commits (only the source file changes).

issue_paraphrase: The robust-fitting routine can compute a nonsensical, non-positive budget for the maximum number of random trials when a very small target probability or a large minimum sample count makes one of the logarithms underflow to one. Instead of always yielding a positive integer number of trials, it can produce zero or a negative value, which makes no sense as an iteration budget. The computed trial count must be guaranteed to be a positive number.
fix_summary: The upstream fix clips both the numerator (1 - probability) and the denominator (1 - inlier_ratio**min_samples) into the range [_EPSILON, 1 - _EPSILON] before taking logarithms, guaranteeing 0 > log value and a positive resulting trial count.
notes: Self-contained, no network, <1 s test. Caveat for the author: the function under test is private (_dynamic_max_trials); the public ransac() only hits the pathological path for extreme inputs (tiny stop_probability with a large min_samples), where in my parent-state probe it still produced sane results, so the direct reproduction goes through the private helper. The public parameter at this vintage is stop_probability (not probability). Because the fix touches only a .py file, only the test file needs to be swapped when authoring. Other tests in test_fit.py pass on era deps; run only the named test to avoid unrelated noise.
